question: Two right prisms have the same height of 10 cm. One has a regular hexagonal base with side 6 cm, and the other has a square base with side 6 cm. What is the ratio of their volumes?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two right prisms have the same height, the ratio of their volumes is strictly equal to the ratio of their base areas.

Ratio = Area of regular hexagonal base : Area of square base

Ratio = [6 × (√3 / 4) × a²] : a²

Since the side length a = 6 cm is identical for both, a² cancels out completely.

Ratio = (3√3 / 2) : 1 = 3√3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3√3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the regular hexagonal base (a) = 6 cm

Side of the square base (b) = 6 cm

Height of both right prisms (h) = 10 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a prism = Area of base × height

Area of a regular hexagon = (3√3 / 2) × (side)²

Area of a square = (side)²

 
 Hexagonal Base a = 6 cm Square Base b = 6 cm Ratio of Volumes = Ratio of Base Areas 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Volume of the hexagonal prism (V₁) = [(3√3 / 2) × 6²] × 10

⇒ V₁ = (3√3 / 2) × 36 × 10

⇒ V₁ = 54√3 × 10 = 540√3 cm³

⇒ Volume of the square prism (V₂) = [6²] × 10

⇒ V₂ = 36 × 10 = 360 cm³

⇒ Ratio of their volumes = V₁ : V₂

⇒ Ratio = 540√3 : 360

⇒ Dividing both sides by 180, we get:

⇒ Ratio = 3√3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3√3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Prism

The volume of any right prism is calculated by multiplying its base area by its height. Formula: V = Base Area × height.

Total Surface Area of a Prism

The total surface area encompasses all the faces of the 3D shape. Formula: TSA = Lateral Surface Area + 2 × Base Area, where Lateral Surface Area = Base Perimeter × height.

Area of a Regular Hexagon

A regular hexagon behaves exactly like 6 adjacent equilateral triangles joined at the center. Area = 6 × (√3 / 4) × side² = (3√3 / 2) × side².
